```{r, include = FALSE}
# chunks run on the example file shipped with the package
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = TRUE)

# ggplot2 is suggested only, so its chunks are skipped when it is absent
has_ggplot2 <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```


This vignette shows how to plot the signals of many reads at once. Two approaches are given: several reads drawn in a single figure, and one image file per read written while the POD5 file is processed in groups. Extraction of single signal is described in `vignette("signal_extraction")`.

First approach keeps all selected signals in memory, so it is suitable for a few to a few dozen reads. Second, based on `process_pod5()`, holds only one group of reads in memory at a time. This is recommended for whole files.


## Example data

All examples below use a small direct RNA sequencing (DRS) file provided with the package.

```{r example-data}

pod5_file <- system.file("extdata", "drs-filtered.pod5",
                         package = "pod5R", mustWork = TRUE)

reader <- pod5R::open_pod5(pod5_file)
reads <- pod5R::read_pod5(reader)

nrow(reads)
```


## Several reads at one figure

### Selecting and extracting reads

Reads are selected from the metadata and extracted with a single `read_pod5()` call. Metadata and signal vectors are returned in the requested order, so the sample rate of each of the reads remain available for the time axis.

```{r extract-reads}

# first six reads in file order
selected_ids <- reads$read_id[1:6]

out <- pod5R::read_pod5(reader,
                        read_ids = selected_ids,
                        signal = TRUE,
                        calibrated = TRUE)

pod5R::close_pod5(reader)

lengths(out[['signal']])
```


### Combining signals into single data frame

ggplot2 expects a single long data frame with one row per sample, so the signals are combined first. The `read_id` column identifies the read each sample comes from. Keep in mind that long reads produce large data frames (here, about `r format(sum(lengths(out[['signal']])), big.mark = ",")` rows). For longer reads, or for many reads, plotting only an interval with `start_sample` and `end_sample` should be considered.


```{r long-data}

signal_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(selected_ids), function(i) {
  read_signal <- out[['signal']][[selected_ids[i]]]
  data.frame(read_id = selected_ids[i],
             # that is how time is rescaled to seconds
             time = (seq_along(read_signal) - 1) / out[['reads']]$sample_rate[i],
             pa = read_signal)
}))

# keep facets in the requested read order
signal_df$read_id <- factor(signal_df$read_id, levels = selected_ids)

head(signal_df, 3)
```

### ggplot2

`facet_wrap()` draws one panel per read. With `scales = "free_x"`, each panel span the full read length, while the current axis is shared, so signal levels can be compared between the reads.

```{r ggplot-facets, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}

g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(signal_df, ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = pa))
g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d")
g.facet <- ggplot2::facet_wrap(~read_id, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x")
g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = "Calibrated signals of selected reads",
                        x = "time [s]",
                        y = "signal [pA]")

plot_reads <- g.base + g.line + g.facet + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()

print(plot_reads)

```

### Base R graphics

In base R, the panel grid is set with `par(mfrow = ...)`. The previous graphical parameters are restored after plotting.

```{r base-grid, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 9}
old_par <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(3, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

for (i in seq_along(selected_ids)) {
  read_signal <- out[['signal']][[selected_ids[i]]]
  graphics::plot((seq_along(read_signal) - 1) / out[['reads']]$sample_rate[i],
                 read_signal,
                 type = "l",
                 col = "#3a414d",
                 xlab = "time [s]",
                 ylab = "signal [pA]",
                 main = substr(selected_ids[i], 1, 8),
                 cex.main = .9)} # for i

graphics::par(old_par)
```

Panel titles show only the first eight characters of each UUID, to keep them short.

## One file per read

### Processing reads in groups

`process_pod5()` reads consecutive groups of `part_size` reads and passes each group to a user-supplied function. With `signal = TRUE`, the function receives a named list with `reads` (metadata) and `signal` (vectors named by UUID). Everything the function returns is discarded, so plots have to be written to files in it. Only one group is held in memory at a time.

In this vignette, plots are written to a temporary directory. For real data,`save_dir` should point to permanent location.

```{r save-dir}
save_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "signal_plots")
if (!dir.exists(save_dir)) {
  dir.create(save_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}
```

> **Note:** `process_pod5()` always reads whole signals. For very long reads,
> a function calling `extract_pod5_signal()` with `start_sample` and
> `end_sample` on selected reads may be a better choice.

### Base R graphics

The function below writes one PNG file per read, named after its UUID:

```{r base-files}
# writes one base R signal plot (png) per read in the group
save_signal_plots_base <- function(batch, save_dir) {
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(batch[['reads']]))) {
    # signal vectors are named by UUID, so look them up by read_id
    read_id <- batch[['reads']]$read_id[i]
    read_signal <- batch[['signal']][[read_id]]

    # open a png device; file named by read UUID with a _base suffix
    grDevices::png(file.path(save_dir, paste0(read_id, "_base.png")),
                   width = 1600, height = 600, res = 150)
    
    # convert sample index to seconds
    graphics::plot((seq_along(read_signal) - 1) / batch[['reads']]$sample_rate[i],
                   read_signal,
                   type = "l",
                   col = "#3a414d",
                   xlab = "time [s]",
                   ylab = "signal [pA]",
                   main = read_id)
    
    grDevices::dev.off()
  } # for i
  
  return(invisible(NULL))
}

pod5R::process_pod5(pod5_file,
                    FUN = save_signal_plots_base,
                    part_size = 10,
                    signal = TRUE,
                    calibrated = TRUE,
                    save_dir = save_dir)

length(list.files(save_dir, pattern = "_base\\.png$"))
```

Any additional arguments given to `process_pod5()` (such as `save_dir` above) are passed to the function.


### ggplot2

The same approach applies with ggplot2, with each plot saved by `ggsave()`:

```{r ggplot-files, eval = has_ggplot2}
# write one ggplot2 signal plot (png) per read in the group
# FUN for process_pod5(), called once per group of reads
save_signal_plots_ggplot <- function(batch, save_dir) {
  
  # seq_len() skips the loop when a group has no reads
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(batch[['reads']]))) {
    # signal vectors are named by UUID, so look them up by read_id
    read_id <- batch[['reads']]$read_id[i]
    read_signal <- batch[['signal']][[read_id]]

    # ggplot2 needs a data frame: one row per sample, time in seconds
    read_df <- data.frame(time = (seq_along(read_signal) - 1) / batch[['reads']]$sample_rate[i],
                          pa = read_signal)

    # layered plot
    g.base <- ggplot2::ggplot(read_df, ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = pa))
    g.line <- ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#3a414d")
    g.labs <- ggplot2::labs(title = read_id,
                            x = "time [s]",
                            y = "signal [pA]")

    plot_signal <- g.base + g.line + g.labs + ggplot2::theme_bw()

    ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(save_dir, paste0(read_id, "_ggplot.png")),
                    plot = plot_signal,
                    width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 150)
  } # for i
  return(invisible(NULL))
}

pod5R::process_pod5(pod5_file,
                    FUN = save_signal_plots_ggplot,
                    part_size = 10,
                    signal = TRUE,
                    calibrated = TRUE,
                    save_dir = save_dir)

length(list.files(save_dir, pattern = "_ggplot\\.png$"))
```


### Selected reads only

To write plots only for a subset of reads, the selection is applied within the function. In the example below, only reads exceeding 20,000 samples are plotted:

```{r selected-files}
# writes base R signal plots only for reads longer than min_samples.
# intended as FUN for process_pod5(), called once per group of reads
save_long_reads <- function(batch, save_dir, min_samples) {
  # flag reads in the current group exceeding defined sample threshold
  keep <- batch[['reads']]$num_samples > min_samples
  if (!any(keep)) {
    return(invisible(NULL)) # no long reads there
  }
  # subset metadata only. Signal list is left as is, as vectors are looked up by read_id
  batch[['reads']] <- batch[['reads']][keep, , drop = FALSE]
  save_signal_plots_base(batch, save_dir)
  
  return(invisible(NULL))
}

long_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "long_reads")
if (!dir.exists(long_dir)) {
  dir.create(long_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

pod5R::process_pod5(pod5_file,
                    FUN = save_long_reads,
                    part_size = 10,
                    signal = TRUE,
                    calibrated = TRUE,
                    verbose = FALSE,
                    save_dir = long_dir,
                    min_samples = 20000)

length(list.files(long_dir))

```

When only a few reads are required from the large file, it is more efficient to select their UUIDs from the `read_pod5()` metadata and extract them directly with `extract_pod5_signal()`. By this, the signals of all the other reads are not decompressed.

## Summary of functions used

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `read_pod5()` | Read metadata; signal with `signal = TRUE` |
| `process_pod5()` | Processing of reads in groups with a user-supplied function |
| `extract_pod5_signal()` | Raw or calibrated signal vectors, optionally an interval |
| `open_pod5()` / `close_pod5()` | Open and close a reusable reader |
